## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `842607546b9d91209c90756ca42ab0a79f6934b6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/filing-gate.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md + scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: ruled

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set and public surface: none moves. The diff is four files, 11 lines in and 11 out: three fleet rule files under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/` and three `CEILINGS` rows in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`. No package, schema, published `skills/**` text or product doc is touched. Right.
- Gate verdicts are the check-runs on this head: 26 success, the rest skipped, none failed or pending. That includes `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, `Check Changeset` and `Test Core`.
- Ratchet rows against the head's bytes (`git show` piped to `wc -c`, a read): `filing-gate.md` 9124 with ceiling 9124; `triage-duties.md` 13709 with ceiling 13709; `execution-duties.md` 22307 with ceiling 22307. On `main` the three files are 9089, 13544 and 22316, so the rows move +35, +165 and −9, each by exactly the landed delta. Both raised rows and the PR body quote ruling record 7135874506 and the delta, as the ratchet header requires for a ruled raise. Right.
- `main` has moved past the PR's merge base (`a73edb3c`), but `git diff` of the head against current `main` on these four files shows only the PR's own 11/11 lines, so the row numbers still describe `main` plus this PR.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: nothing in the diff is published. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body matches the tree (no schema, no authorable surface, no narrowing). `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report carries no `open_questions`. Its deviations that touch the contract, each answered:

- A1's 「人定的级除外」 is not in the ruling's words. Accepted; see N1. Without it the new clause would contradict `filing-gate.md` line 38 (an objection to a human-set grade is one comment line, grade and card state untouched), since `pm:retriage` blocks dispatch and so changes the card's state. On human-graded cards the head behaves exactly as `main` does.
- B7 lives only in `triage-duties.md` and `filing-gate.md` does not repeat it. Accepted: the line says 「分诊任一关卡路径」, which reaches the missing-parts close in `filing-gate.md` line 45 and the tooling and outside-the-three-classes closes in `triage-duties.md` lines 74 and 100–101. Only the p3 standard claimed to win over keep rules, and it now excepts the line.
- PR body carries both `Part of #35855 (items …)` and `Refs #35855 (items …)`. Neither is a closing keyword, they name the same items, and the PR-body guards check is success on this head. The card correctly stays open for A5. No effect on the contract.
- The dev ran 43 local gate commands; those are the dev's own and are not adopted here. This record reads the check-runs only.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff has no code path that reads data.

Rule change: the PR body declares `Rule-change: ruled` with `Ruling-ref: 7135874506 — 「照推荐：采纳 5 条」`. Each rule hunk was checked against the ruling comment's own item text:

- A1: 「评论抬严重度或可达面同笔挂 `pm:retriage` …,分诊答复定级,⛔ 立卡人不改」 copies "a comment that raises severity or reach also carries the existing `pm:retriage` label, so triage's existing reader … answer it". No new key, no North Star exception, as ruled.
- B4: 「本文「折叠」除 `Fold-with:` 外皆指此并卡,⛔ 不过派发折叠五门与五卡上限」 copies "a triage fold is a merge of cards, not a dispatch fold under the five fold gates". The five-card cap is part of the same gate line in `execution-duties.md` (「折叠准入五门全过即默认折(≤5 卡)」), not a separate rule.
- B7: the evaluation line copies "the evaluation keep applies to every triage close path, not only the p3 first-touch standard".
- C1: the `Size/model suggestion:` wording and the `size/l` spelling are deleted; the audit comment's `· size XS|S|M|L` stays as the one scale.

Three clauses go beyond the ruling's words: 「人定的级除外」 (A1), 「并入他卡或周清扫卡照行」 (B7) and 「(下条除外)」 (the p3 standard). Each one holds an existing behaviour of `main` in place or removes a contradiction the ruled line would otherwise create. None lets an agent do anything `main` did not already allow. So `ruled` stands.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`filing-gate.md` (A1). The clause uses `pm:retriage` inside its existing definition: SKILL.md's state table lists 改判 as a use, and `state-machine.md` requires the label and the objection comment in one write (「同笔」, as the new clause says), has triage answer and remove it each fire, and keeps the old grade authoritative until then. The card in this branch is unclaimed or the filer's own, so the dispatch block that comes with the label lands on no other seat's work. Holds.

`triage-duties.md` (B4). Every 折叠 on the head was read: line 64 (照折叠关卡, the weekly ADR card move), line 83 (照折叠关卡, the weekly sweep card move), line 86 (the `Fold-with:` line, both uses, excepted by its key), line 92 (the new clause itself) and line 93 (永不折叠或移卡). Lines 64 and 83 borrow the merge's manner of closing (close `duplicate`, the close line names the claim), which is what 此并卡 gives them. Line 93 must be the triage merge: read as a dispatch fold it would forbid folding `security` cards, which `lanes/security.md` line 31 does by group under the five gates. No use is mis-defined; the clause removes that ambiguity.

`triage-duties.md` (B7 and the p3 standard). 「下条」 is the next bullet, line 63, the evaluation line; the p3 bullet ends at line 62. With the evaluation item out of the 留条 list and the exception in, the p3 standard gives the same answer as on `main`. The other close paths (lines 74, 100, 101; `filing-gate.md` line 45) are narrowed by the universal wording and none claims precedence, so none contradicts it. Close `duplicate` (merge) and close `completed` (line 96) stay open, which matches `main`, where the never-fold list on line 93 does not name evaluation cards.

`triage-duties.md` and `execution-duties.md` (C1). On the head, `git grep` over `.claude/**` and `AGENTS.md` for `size/`, `Size/model` and `suggestion` returns nothing; on `main` it returned exactly the three lines this PR edits. The remaining `size/l` strings in the repository are the PR size labeler (`scripts/pr-labels.mjs`, workflows, label-write fixtures), a different label family the ruling does not touch. `execution-duties.md` line 173 now reads 「分诊 size 是输入不是决定」, which agrees with `triage-duties.md` line 84 (size is a reference, the claim may change it). No stale reference is left behind.

`scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`. The three rows agree with the files, as measured in ①. Each raise is at most the landed delta and names the ruling id and items; the lowered row needs no ruling.

Nits, none affecting correctness:

- N1 (nit) — A1's 「人定的级除外」 narrows the ruling: a severity-raising comment on a human-graded card still has no reader beyond the comment itself, which is the gap item A1 named. This is unchanged from `main` and is the conservative reading, because the alternative lets a seat's label override line 38. Whether A1 should reach human-graded cards is the maintainer's call. Card #35855 stays open for A5, so say it there in one line; do not fix it in this PR.
- N2 (nit) — 「(下条除外)」 points by position. A later line inserted between lines 62 and 63 would repoint the exception with no gate to catch it. A follow-up could name the line by its subject (评测条) at about the same byte cost.
- N3 (nit) — after C1 the effort section reads the triage size directly, and `execution-duties.md` line 167 (untouched by this diff) maps S, M, L and XL but not XS, while triage's scale has no XL. An XS card falls to 「拿不准 ⇒ `high`」 on a literal read. Outside this diff; follow-up card material.
- N4 (nit) — B7 says an evaluation card is not closed not_planned on the tooling close path (line 74) but gives it no landing there; such a card can neither enter `pm:queue` without one of the three doors nor close. The merge and weekly-list routes cover it in practice.

<details><summary>Brief</summary>

## Contract review brief — PR #37030 @ `842607546b9d91209c90756ca42ab0a79f6934b6` (card #35855)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35855: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37030: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `842607546b9d91209c90756ca42ab0a79f6934b6`
  · the check-runs on `842607546b9d91209c90756ca42ab0a79f6934b6`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/filing-gate.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/25fb535a-733b-5351-a141-2940135fc987/scratchpad/pr-37030/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.
